title: Practice with a partner
hookLine: a shared ritual with someone you love: Tobias asked Sarah to rise and pray with him, and she said the amen too
tomorrow: what did Jesus do when his friends shooed the kids away?

cards: Sunday pancakes, the walk after dinner, the same song in the car: a couple's one thing that's theirs. The book of Tobit has a couple whose first night needed more than a song.

Sarah had been married seven times, and each time, on the wedding night, a demon named Asmodeus killed the husband. Now Tobias has married her, guided by a traveling companion who is secretly the angel Raphael.
The door shuts. Before morning, her father will be outside, digging a grave.

teach.b: Tobias does what Raphael told him. He lays the heart and liver of a fish on the coals of the incense, and the smoke drives the demon off.

teach.h: SISTER, ARISE, AND LET US PRAY.
teach.b: Then, before anything else, he gets up and says: "Sister, arise, and let us pray that God would have pity on us." He doesn't pray over her while she watches. He asks her to rise with him.
His prayer remembers Adam, and Eve given to him as a helper and a stay, and asks "that we may become aged together."

teach.h: AND SHE SAID WITH HIM, AMEN.
teach.b: And then the line that makes it shared: "And she said with him, Amen." Two voices, one amen. In the morning, the grave gets filled back in.

So what does the story teach? Tobit is a Jewish story, kept in the Bibles of Catholic and Orthodox Christians; the Jewish Bible doesn't include it, and Protestant Bibles that print it set it among the Apocrypha.
Catholic wedding readings include this very prayer.

teach.h: A MARRIAGE BEGUN WITH A SHARED PRAYER.
teach.b: In the story, a marriage starts with two people standing up together and asking for the same thing, out loud. Not one partner's practice with the other one watching.
For two people now, it can be very small: one line before dinner, a candle, a walk where each of you names one good thing. What makes it practice with a partner is the amen. Both of you say yes.

how: Couples on many paths keep small shared rituals: a blessing before a meal, candles on Friday night, a prayer or a thank-you said together at bedtime. Tobias and Sarah's prayer from Tobit 8 is among the readings offered for Catholic weddings.

games.q: what does “practice with a partner” mean?
o: one person's private routine, done while the other waits
a counseling session for couples led by a spiritual coach
a small ritual two people share, both saying yes to it

games.q: Tobias and Sarah: tap the pairs.
p: the demon of Sarah's wedding nights
the angel disguised as a traveling companion
sister, arise, and let us pray

s: in Tobit, Tobias prays alone while Sarah watches
he asks her to rise and pray with him, and she says the amen with him.
Tobit is in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles but not in the Jewish Bible
it's a Jewish story; Protestant Bibles that print it set it among the Apocrypha.
Tobias's prayer asks for riches and a long line of heirs
it asks for mercy, and "that we may become aged together."

games.q: a friend wants a nightly ritual with her partner, who isn't religious. by Tobit 8, what's the first move?
o: ask him to join a short shared line that both of them can say yes to.
keep doing her own practice in front of him until he decides to copy it.
wait until the two of them agree on every belief before trying anything.
games.why: Tobias didn't perform his prayer for Sarah. He asked her to rise with him, and the amen was hers too.

practice: Write one small thing you could share with someone you love: a line, a walk, a candle, a meal. Keep it short enough for two people to say yes to. Then sit tall, the way Tobias stood up first, and let the breath come and go.

wordCard.voice: Practice with a partner: a small ritual two people share, both saying yes to it, like Tobias and Sarah's one amen.

orig.note: Hebrew: 'so be it', 'truly'. The word Sarah said with Tobias, from the Jewish and Christian scriptures.

carryVoice: Your line: together. Two voices, and one amen at the end. Day 1653, and a new stretch begins: others.
